name: Sprocket
text: Do a shadow test on the new prompt before rolling it out. This lets us catch hidden flaws by replaying real traffic without affecting users, which is safer than live A/B tests. The trade-off is delayed rollout while we validate, but the risk of breaking user experience is far lower.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow testing misses silent failures—like a prompt that degrades answers over time without crashing. A better alternative is canary deployments with real-time metrics: roll out to 5% of users, monitor for drift in quality or latency, and auto-rollback on anomalies. Settle it by running a 24-hour canary with the same traffic volume as a full rollout and comparing error rates.

name: Gauge
text: Canary deployments still miss silent failures—like a prompt that degrades answers for a niche user segment not in the 5%. A better alternative is staged rollouts with *adaptive sampling*: monitor *all* traffic but only expose the new prompt to users whose behavior matches the worst-case degradation patterns we’ve seen before.
